report.answer_text:
Lenacapavir is an antiretroviral drug made by Gilead Sciences. It is an HIV-1 capsid inhibitor, meaning it interferes with the protein shell (capsid) that HIV needs to replicate. It is long-acting and is given as a subcutaneous injection about every six months, with oral tablets used when starting. It was first approved in 2022 as Sunlenca to treat HIV-1 infection in people whose virus is resistant to other drugs.
2025 FDA approval: On June 18, 2025, the FDA approved lenacapavir under the brand name Yeztugo. It is approved as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg. It is described as the first and only HIV prevention option that gives six months of protection per dose.
Evidence: The approval rested on two phase 3 trials, PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2. In both, at least 99.9% of participants on twice-yearly Yeztugo stayed HIV-negative. PURPOSE 1 reported no HIV infections among 2,134 participants in the lenacapavir group.
Sources: Drugs.com (Yeztugo approval history) and HCPLive (June 18, 2025).
